A country made for wandering

Pakistan holds three great mountain ranges, the Karakoram, the Himalaya and the Hindu Kush, within a single border. Glacial rivers carve green valleys, turquoise lakes sit beneath white peaks, and high plateaus bloom with wildflowers every summer.

The landscape is matched by its people. Hospitality is a point of pride here: expect to be invited for chai, offered the best seat, and sent off with stories and directions. Ancient Gandhara monasteries, Mughal-era forts and the colour of truck art and hand-woven shawls make every region feel distinct.

Tourism is growing, with better roads, family-run guesthouses and local guides who know every trail. It’s a good time to see it before everyone else does.

Travel tips

Practical advice for a smoother, safer and more respectful trip.

☀️

Best time to visit

May to October is the main season for the north. Skardu and Deosai are best from June to September; Swat is lovely in spring and autumn. Many high roads and passes close in winter.

🎒

What to pack

Layers, a windproof jacket, broken-in hiking shoes, sunscreen, sunglasses, a power bank and any medicines you need. Add a warm hat and gloves for altitudes above 3,000 m.

🛡️

Travel safety

Check road, weather and security advisories before each leg. Use licensed local guides for treks, keep copies of your ID, carry cash for remote areas and share your plans with someone.

🚐

Transportation

Fly from Islamabad to Gilgit or Skardu (weather dependent), or take the Karakoram Highway by road. Hire a 4x4 and driver for Fairy Meadows, Deosai and Naltar; landslides can cause delays, so keep a spare day.

🤝

Respect local culture

Dress modestly, ask before photographing people, remove shoes where asked and be mindful during prayer times and Ramadan. A greeting of “Assalam-o-Alaikum” goes a long way.
